solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ambience? A most peculiar piano in this place

indicators.note: something peculiar is odd or out of shape, so the letters of the word most are jumbled

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano (softly)

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the strange mood of a room where a piano stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' makes TMOS from MOST; with A in front, P for piano and HERE after it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere is the mood or feeling of a place, which is just what ambience means.

clue.text: Recording almost entirely useless, from America

parts.note: bum is American slang for worthless, as in a bum deal

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses an American recording as almost entirely useless.
explanation.walkthrough: "From America" flags that BUM is being used in its US adjective sense, not the British one.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a recording issued as a collection of tracks.

clue.text: Answer not hard to see in golf? Male coming over, being patronising?

definitions.note: the verb phrase 'being patronising' stands for the -ing form describing what a man does

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece coming over the rest sits on top of it

parts.note: ans. is the standard abbreviation for answer
G is golf in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A man at the golf course condescendingly explains something that was obvious anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's first words look like the start, but M for "Male" goes on top of everything else because this is a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansplaining is a man explaining something in a patronising way, usually to a woman who already knows it.

clue.text: Second family hide

parts.note: s = second, the unit of time

explanation.surface: A second family has to go into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: "Hide" looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the leather-trade sense: a tanner works an animal's pelt whether you call it the hide or the skin.

clue.text: Meal for Macbeth? Witches bringing in good one

indicators.note: bringing something in means taking it inside, so the letters go within

parts.note: hags are ugly old women, especially witches
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The witches in Macbeth fetching one decent meal for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is Scotland's national dish, so a fitting supper for a Scottish king; the question mark flags the playful example.

clue.text: Rare slip after arranging retaliation

indicators.note: the letters are what you have after arranging them anew

explanation.surface: An unusual mistake draws a vengeful response once someone has sorted things out.
explanation.walkthrough: "After arranging" reads as a time phrase in the surface, but it tells you to rearrange RARE SLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name a hitting back at an enemy for harm done, as when a raid provokes reprisals.

clue.text: Film comedian repaired broken statue

indicators.note: a repaired thing has had its parts put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A film comedian mends a statue that has been smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: "Broken" is not the indicator here but part of the fodder; "repaired" does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton was a star comedian of silent films.

clue.text: Regret a lot of painful argument

indicators.note: most but not all, so the last letter of the word for painful is dropped

explanation.surface: Remorse over much of a bitter quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Painful here is the adjective sore, not suffering, and argument is a quarrel rather than a line of reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow is grief or sadness, and regret is the sadness felt over something done.

clue.text: Suggestion from republican finance industry?

definitions.meaning: split in two, it is the proposal an anti-monarchist would make: get rid of the monarch
the business of lending, deposits and loans, taken as a whole sector

explanation.surface: A republican proposes something about the banking sector.
explanation.walkthrough: A republican here means someone opposed to monarchy, whose suggestion would be to BAN (the) KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Banking is the business of banks, the core of the finance industry.

clue.text: Start to patronise London airport skipping new destination for extended flight?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here taken from patronise
skipping means leaving out, so a letter is dropped from the airport's name

parts.note: Luton is an airport serving London

explanation.surface: A traveller flies out of a London airport bound for some far-off place on a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is one of London's airports; 'skipping new' drops its N to leave LUTO, after P from 'Start to patronise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto, the distant dwarf planet, would be the goal of a very long space mission, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Be glum as motorcycle loses rear end

indicators.note: the word's back end, its last letter, is lost

parts.note: a moped is a small low-powered motorcycle

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy because their motorbike has lost its back end.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to be listless and dejected, sulking in low spirits.

clue.text: Spray enveloping popular member of cabinet

indicators.note: the outer word wraps round the inner one

parts.note: a mister is a device that sprays fine droplets

explanation.surface: A popular politician is caught in a spray, perhaps of protest.
explanation.walkthrough: "Spray" is the noun for the spraying gadget, not the droplets.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the cabinet is the group of senior government heads of department, each holding that title.

clue.text: Very precise individual line in adhesive label

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: a sticker is an adhesive label

explanation.surface: A pedant insists that a label carry a single exact line.
explanation.walkthrough: "Individual" is a noun here, part of the definition, not an adjective describing the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler is someone who insists on exactness.

clue.text: Cordiality and warmth welcoming traveller at last

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece is placed inside the other
at last points to the final letter of traveller

explanation.surface: A traveller arriving is greeted with friendliness and warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts R, the last letter of traveller, inside HEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart can mean warmth of feeling or kindness, as in having a lot of heart, so it matches friendliness.

clue.text: Religious book extreme elements of holy men are loving at the outset

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of holy
first and last letters of men

indicators.note: the outset of each word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The book says holy men are loving from the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: Two different selectors share the clue: outer letters for the first two words, first letters for the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a book of hymns used in church.

clue.text: Missile transporter missing opening

indicators.note: without its first letter, so the barrow loses its start

parts.note: a barrow is a cart for carrying loads, a transporter

explanation.surface: A rocket launcher whose hatch has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing opening' drops the B of BARROW.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a projectile shot from a bow, a basic missile.

clue.text: Annoys park wardens, blowing top

indicators.note: losing the top letter, which in a down answer is the first

parts.note: rangers look after parks and forests

explanation.surface: Wardens in a park lose their temper and irritate people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' sounds like losing one's temper but means dropping the first letter of RANGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger someone is to annoy or enrage them, so angers matches annoys.

clue.text: Intimidating blokes acting out of turn to begin with

parts.note: blokes is British slang for men

indicators.note: out of means without, so a letter is removed from acting
to begin with points to the first letter of turn

explanation.surface: Some men play their parts badly, coming in before their cue, and it unsettles everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to begin with' takes T from turn, and 'out of' removes it from ACTING to leave ACING, after MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something menacing is threatening, the same sense as intimidating.

clue.text: Unproductive, with no soil, with no carbon

indicators.note: takes the cut letters out of the word

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Land is barren because it has no soil and no carbon in it.
explanation.walkthrough: "With no soil" feels like part of a barren field; it is CLEAN, unsoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean year or season is one that produces little.

clue.text: Appropriate place, hot, in French resort

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
h = hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A tourist finds a suitably hot spot in Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling Nice is the capitalised French city, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a place or role that suits someone.

clue.text: Asian resort erected one experimental location

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means set upright, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a lab is where experiments are done

explanation.surface: An Asian holiday spot puts up a single research facility.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed LAB comes first even though "one" is written before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Cancel regular publication after second article rejected

indicators.note: the article is rejected, thrown out of the word

parts.note: a book or magazine issued once a year
a is the indefinite article; the second A in the word is the one thrown out

explanation.surface: An editor cancels a yearly magazine after its second article is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: "Second article" means the second A in ANNUAL, not a second piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: a court that annuls a marriage cancels it, declaring it void.

clue.text: Flexible element in the last ice-cap

indicators.note: the answer is an element, a part, found in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something pliable is found in the last polar ice-cap.
explanation.walkthrough: "Element" suggests chemistry, but here it just means a part of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both adjectives, used of materials and figuratively of rules or schedules that bend.

clue.text: Foresight regarding Southern Channel Islands during change

indicators.note: these letters come during the other word, inside it

explanation.surface: A forecaster predicts how currency in the southern Channel Islands will change.
explanation.walkthrough: PENCE are British coins, the everyday small change in one's pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescience is knowing about things before they happen.
